title: Phase 1 complete: design settled
summary: Distilled two source systems into one generalizable .claude operating system after five analysis deep-dives and one adversarial review verified against real captured hook events.

title: Eight design decisions settled
summary: Sibling-folder RECORD_ROOT, allowlist redaction with raw kept forever, plain HTML console, commit-always push-ask, spines-only layers, one full profile with soft and hard evolution gears, stdlib core with uv as the extension tier, JSON handshake envelopes.

title: Thesis: three surfaces, one place each
summary: One place to interact (Claude Code), one place to control (the console), one command to evolve (/project-memory), on an always-on record behind fail-closed gates. Observability and governance are substrate, not surfaces.

title: Phase 2 foundation: _lib, configs, hooks, ritual runner
summary: Shared foundation with two-tier atomic writes and one journal vocabulary; five hooks split fail-closed (gates) from fail-open (telemetry); checkctl runs the ritual with a transaction checkpoint and a content-hash generator ledger.

title: Sub-agent bash denylist leaked to the main session
summary: policy.default.deny_bash applied to the orchestrator too, so the main session was denied git. Caught by the hooks smoke test before it ever ran live; the default block now applies to sub-agent identities only.

title: Phase 2 complete: the system runs on itself
summary: All 37 components built and probed, 140 tests green, and the full ritual (check, polish, publish) runs on this repo as one transaction. The record captured this session's own construction: 140k output tokens attributed across four models.

title: Opus adversarial code review found 3 critical and 7 important defects
summary: Review verified every finding empirically against the running system. Its central criticism was that docstrings asserted properties the code did not deliver, and that the 125 green tests confirmed the narrative rather than attacking it. All findings fixed, each with a regression test.

title: The policy gate could be switched off by writing a large file
summary: The hook passed the payload through an environment variable, which Linux caps at 128KB. A Write payload carries the file's whole content, so writing over ~128KB to a protected path made execve fail, python never ran, no decision was emitted, and the harness read silence as allow. Now the payload goes via a temp file and a non-zero judge exit fails closed.

title: Sealing silently destroyed distinct raw events
summary: Event identity was a second-precision timestamp plus fields hook events do not carry, so parallel sub-agents finishing in the same second collapsed into one row, discarding the rest from the tier documented as kept forever. A capture-time uniquifier now makes each event distinct.

title: The seal allowlist filtered key names but not values
summary: An allowlisted key holding a nested structure passed through verbatim, so a secret nested under an allowed field reached the redacted tier. Structured values are now replaced by shape markers; the verbatim original stays in out-of-repo raw.

title: Protected tree extended to every directory the gate executes from
summary: The gate imports _lib from .claude/tools on every tool call, but tools/, skills/ and console/ were unprotected, so a sub-agent could write the gate's own dependency and own it on the next call.

title: Human-agent bridge: required context/action + copy-context button
summary: need open now mechanically requires --context and --action written for a human reading cold; the console renders both per item with a copy button producing a paste-ready reply ending in 'My answer:'. Enforced in statectl, not by a sub-agent: the smallest primitive that guarantees the behavior.

title: Structured-output analysis engine
summary: obsctl analyze is now one OpenAI-compatible protocol (OpenRouter/Ollama/OpenAI/vLLM) with parallel chunked calls, json_schema structured output with fallback, repair, and mechanical taxonomy validation. Key from env only; labels fold into the story feed's analysis lane by plain code; the console gained its single POST action endpoint for it.

title: System map focus mode
summary: Click a component to fade everything unconnected and raise its neighborhood to the front; second click opens the detail popup; Esc clears. The connections are now traceable, which was the map's weakest point in first use.

title: Adoption smoke test: mechanics sound, nine frictions found
summary: A sub-agent adopted the system into a scratch repo by following /adopt literally: 37/37 probe, record isolated to the target's sibling, tests green. It also found two policy-gate bugs by dogfooding (git-path false positive, cross-project .claude-iff denial) and four skill gaps (CLAUDE.md instantiation unstated, unpassable placeholder grep, card-pruning wording that would delete core anatomy, mislabeled hooks-fire probe). All fixed with regression tests.

title: The governance held on real work
summary: The console sub-agent was denied writes to the protected .claude/console/ tree by the policy gate and returned its template as a proposal; the main session reviewed and applied it. The protected-tree mechanism proved itself unprompted on the first real multi-agent task after the hardening.

title: Distribution: two zips, a registered generator, and a release workflow
summary: distctl.py builds dot-claude-iff-fresh.zip and dot-claude-iff-adopt-kit.zip deterministically (fixed timestamps, write-gated) as a registered generator, so releases can never lag the repo. A GitHub Actions workflow tests then releases both on any v* tag.

title: README: stable work blocks + human collaboration guide + layout illustration
summary: Two sections teach the human half of the contract (brief like a colleague, answer via copy-context, debug with evidence, correct once then make it stick, close your blocks), with the side-by-side SVG showing the recommended layout across terminal, VS Code and desktop.

title: Billing mode: subscription is a truth, not an unknown
summary: model-prices.json gained billing api|subscription. Under subscription, dollar cost is not applicable: the empty-table warning goes quiet, the console reads 'in plan', and token counts keep flowing. Default set to subscription for this repo and the shipped zips.

title: Multi-page guided tour with progress tracking
summary: The docs tour is now ten pages (start, understand, setup, six exercises, finish) with shared tour.css/tour.js: a progress bar, per-page dots persisted in localStorage, prev/next and arrow-key navigation, all relative-linked so it works on Pages and over file://.

title: Demo console on the docs site
summary: docs/demo/console.html is the real console snapshotted from this repo by a new demo_build generator, flagged serverless so it badges 'demo snapshot' instead of polling. A visitor clicks the real 49-component map before installing anything.

title: README rebuilt around the six architecture decisions
summary: Verb-led front page: what it does in six verbs, then the decisions (context-carrying communication, managed memory, the progress pulse, one command to stop-publish-learn-evolve, the self-explaining map, merge-never-takeover adoption), a see-it table, star and issue links held to the system's own communication contract.

title: Showcase polish round: hero titles, one-line buttons, map legend, colored footer, motto pair
summary: Hero gained colored pane titles (console ocean, Claude Code orange) with matching dashes; three depth-styled buttons in one line with the Partner Guide banner beneath; the MAP tab opens with a kind-color legend; the console footer puts the timestamp and orange token total far left and the three colored links far right; both mottoes close the README and tour.

title: Edge colors are a disjoint family from node kinds
summary: Connections recolored to purples and pink (writes violet solid, reads light-purple dashed, invokes pink solid) so a line's hue can never be misread as a node's role; both legends now sit at the top of the MAP tab. The implemented relation taxonomy stays reads/writes/invokes from the card schema; feedback, human and validates remain reserved renderer styles to be promoted into card fields via evolution when real evidence needs them.

title: Showcase iteration round with the maintainer
summary: Live feedback loop over the public face: hero rebuilt with the triad annotations on top (control blue, remember green, interact orange) over the dashed side-by-side; responsive one-line blue buttons; dashed Partner Guide banner restored; keywords strip moved under the why paragraph; habits numbered in the guide and mirrored as a README dropdown with the maintainer's personal ADHD-household note.

title: Edge palette settled monochrome, superseding the purple family
summary: Connection colors went purple/pink first, then settled as black writes, dashed-black reads, gray invokes: node kinds keep the only hues on the map, edges read as pure structure. Relation taxonomy stays reads/writes/invokes; feedback, human and validates remain reserved styles pending evidence.

title: Tour top navigation and analysis card placement
summary: One row under the header divider: labeled Prev far left, centered clickable progress dots, labeled Next far right; the Retrospective analysis card moved to the end of STORY with a what-it-is and how-it-works info box, and its setup guide deduplicated.

title: v0.1.1 released
summary: Tag pushed, workflow green in 31 seconds, both zips attached and marked Latest. The release carries the tour, demo console, Partner Guide, analysis engine and the brand pass. An ultrareview of the branch delta returned zero findings.

title: Button wrap shipped: local screenshot check used a wider container than GitHub's
summary: The three README buttons at fixed 280px passed a 900px local render but wrapped to two lines on GitHub's real container; the maintainer caught it by screenshot. Fixed with percentage widths (31% each), which sidestep the container-width question entirely.

title: Evolution P1: theme-token-parity CHECK step
summary: First real retro proposal implemented: checkctl asserts the console template's two dark blocks define the identical custom-property set, turning the twice-in-one-day L-7 bug class into a ritual failure. Registered in phases.check with regression tests including a proof the shipped template passes its own gate.

title: Evolution P2: the width miss logged as lesson L-8
summary: Second retro proposal: the shipped visual defect became a lesson with a mechanical prevention (percentage widths for README assets; when fixed pixels are unavoidable, render local checks at or below 830px content width).

title: v0.2.0: the first post-evolution release
summary: Minor bump because the shipped system changed, not just its docs: the theme-parity ritual gate from the first real retro, the map's dual legends and monochrome edges, the console footer links and token total, the analysis info box, and the tour navigation. system_version now moves with the tag so adopters' drift warning keys correctly.

title: v0.2.1 - field-report hardening
summary: Fixed all confirmed findings from the first three real adoptions (issues #1-#3): Windows durable-write crash, distribution privacy leaks gated behind memory.json distribution.enabled with kits shipping it false and a git-tracked payload manifest, adopt-skill surgery (CLAUDE.md exclusion, history guard, sibling mode, decide-once console port), task-reality tokenizer, store.dist declaration, symbolic-ref removed from the read-only carve-out in both policy spots, gitignore-shadow lint, loud console port collisions.

title: Logo embedded across the three public surfaces
summary: The maintainer's spiral-of-people logo landed as docs/assets/logo.png with two derived assets: a one-row README footer pairing it with the joined motto, favicons plus topbar marks on all ten tour pages, and demo-only branding on the published console. The local console stays unbranded - the favicon and banner logo are injected behind the DATA.demo flag, so a machine's own console never gains web chrome.

title: The console build write-gate compared a subset of what it writes
summary: consolectl build compared payloads, not rendered pages, so a template edit with an unchanged payload never reached the output while the generator ledger marked it fresh; a wall-clock heartbeat age also made every build rewrite. Now it compares the full render, masking only generated_at and now.heartbeat_age_seconds.

title: Release changelog pinning, gated to the home repo
summary: CHANGELOG.md at the repo root (backfilled from every existing tag) plus a changelog_parity CHECK step that fails the ritual when a tag or the stamped system_version lacks its section, and a release recipe in the project-memory skill. Adopters never see any of it: the file sits outside the .claude/ tree the zips and the adopt skill copy, and the check rides the same distribution.enabled knob as the home-only generators.

title: The policy gate failed OPEN on Windows
summary: Four independent holes, all live in real sessions on this platform: the protected-tree ring built a backslash relative path and compared it to posix prefixes (so a sub-agent could write hooks, tools and configs); the record ring's mention regex could not capture drive-letter paths; the post-write validator exited before validating anything; and the PowerShell tool was absent from the PreToolUse matcher, leaving every ring open to one lane. Fixed with posix/normcase comparisons, case-folding where the filesystem is case-insensitive, and PowerShell judged like Bash.

title: Windows portability of the tools and the suite
summary: obsctl's transcript slug converted only '/' and '.', so ingest matched nothing on Windows and token tracking was silently empty; _lib.rel and _lib.tilde emitted backslash display paths that would have rewritten every card and console string on a Windows session. Both now normalize. The suite went from a fifth of it failing to fully green on this platform.

title: Console ports derive from the folder name
summary: The shipped default became "auto": each project derives a stable port from a hash of its folder name (7100-7899, walking forward on a collision) and the console answers on http://<folder>.localhost:<port>/ as well as the loopback IP. This retires the decide-a-port-per-project step and the everyone-collides-on-one-default problem; an explicit integer remains a decided-once override that still fails loudly. Rejected the alternative of one shared daemon serving every project by path: it needs global mutable state and puts all projects in one browser origin.

title: Optional system monitor and device identity
summary: sysmon.py probes CPU, RAM and NVIDIA GPU/VRAM with stdlib only, per-OS, failing open per metric; console.py serves it at /live/system.json behind an opt-in knob and the NOW tab renders a strip between needs-human and the journal. The samples are live-only by construction, so no committed surface or published demo can carry a machine's stats. Alongside it, state/machine.json records a salted user|host fingerprint and a human-chosen alias - never a username or hostname - and the session-start hook compares read-only, printing a loud DEVICE CHANGE line until statectl device names the box.

title: Stray runtime files written into the committed record surface
summary: A hand-rolled console launch used the wrong directory helper and dropped a pidfile and an empty log into .claude-iff/ instead of RECORD_ROOT. The gate correctly refused to delete them from the shell; they were removed with a disclosed script and journaled. The lesson is narrow: a manual launch of a service must mirror the hook's own paths rather than re-deriving them.

title: v0.2.2 - Windows gate hardening and a console that knows its machine
summary: Released with both distribution zips attached and the changelog section as its notes. Carries the Windows security fixes, the changelog machinery, derived console ports, the optional system monitor, device identity, and the logo. First release cut through the new recipe in the project-memory skill, and the first where changelog_parity gated the tag.

title: v0.3.0-alpha.2 - Cview-ready backbone (worktree sessions are workers)
summary: Cut from dev and published as a GitHub pre-release by release.yml (suite green on ubuntu and windows, both zips attached, latest unchanged). A session started inside a linked worktree is detected by _lib.worktree_info and treated as a worker: WORKTREE SESSION block, main-anchored record root, state writes refused, gate rings, Stop-hook advisory, two CLAUDE.md role sections.

title: A worker keeps write access to its copy of the protected tree
summary: Departure from extrct_private's version, which denies hooks/tools/config to a worker: here builders already edit those in dispatch worktrees and the lead reviews before accept merges, and under Cview the main session's /code-review plays that role. What a worker cannot do: dispatch/accept, write .claude/state/ (handshakes excepted), open the ritual.

title: One record per project: the record root anchors at the main checkout from a worktree
summary: A worktree under .claude/worktrees/ has no sibling worth writing to; capture from worker sessions lands in the project's one record. Relative record_root values anchor at main too; the env override still wins.

title: The journal's projections are gitignored; the journal stays tracked
summary: session.json, HANDOFF.md and needs-human.json joined the managed .gitignore block and were untracked in the home repo, so a checkout that only ran a session ends clean (Cview's merge refuses a dirty main) and a worktree's stale copy never merges back. Existing adoptions rerun gitignore --apply and git rm --cached the three once.

title: No Claude Code marketplace plugin; the kit stays a .claude/ drop-in
summary: A plugin installs outside the repo, where the gate's rings, per-project evolution and the worker rules do not reach. A thin installer plugin may be revisited after the stable 0.3. User-confirmed.

title: License Apache-2.0; CITATION.cff; both LICENSE and NOTICE ship inside .claude/ of every kit
summary: The repo had no license at all. Apache over MIT for the trademark clause and explicit obligations. The kits carry LICENSE and NOTICE inside .claude/ so they license the system, never the adopter's project; changelog_parity now fails when CITATION.cff's version lags system_version. Title and author fields confirmed by the maintainer (ORCID, Independent, Switzerland).

title: Road-to-beta checklist with a place for every step
summary: docs/alpha-test-checklist.md rewritten: four named places (main session, your terminal, browser, elsewhere), Do/Expect per box, what alpha.2 already evidenced live, beta criteria, and item 10 for the worktree session.

title: Issues 10, 14, 16, 17, 18 reviewed against alpha.2; replies drafted, not posted
summary: #10 largely answered by the managed block; #16 partly (TASK.md Owns and the state ring), the rest belongs to the parallel variant; #17 narrowed by the no-plugin decision; #18 is the seam alpha.2 builds (one detector, no Cview dependency). Posting waits for the maintainer.

title: The session ran in a stale secondary clone (GIT/_sources/dot-claude-iff)
summary: The terminal's cwd was a second clone made 2026-10-09 for analysis; nothing in Cview or the system chose it. Consequences: the maintainer's VS Code (on GIT/dot-claude-iff) could not see the new files, today's capture landed in an empty record root, and three dev commits sat unpushed in the wrong clone. Fix: push, pull the canonical clone, copy the spool across, delete the stray clone.

title: Backticked Cview file names in CLAUDE.md tripped context_health twice
summary: TASK.md, DONE.md, BLOCKED.md, .cview/ and .claude/state/ in backticks read as dead paths (they do not exist in this repo or in the kit). The lint caught it in the suite, then again in the kit self-test. Prose names for files the system reads but never ships.

title: Chrome extension unreachable; console verified over HTTP only
summary: Three attempts to attach the Claude Chrome extension failed, so item 4 of the checklist (the console in a browser) keeps only its HTTP evidence: the page and the live payload answer 200 with no warnings.

title: Code graph for the console: graphify measured, GitDiagram is the target
summary: Graphify (tree-sitter, local, no model) was run on this repo by the maintainer and its real schema recorded; its viewer is a CDN force graph with no click-to-source and no organisation. The maintainer's reference turned out to be GitDiagram: a curated subsystem diagram with boxes linked to source. Design revised to one architecture spec per scope, rendered to Mermaid in docs and to the console MAP renderer; graphify becomes the src/ skeleton and the drill-down.

title: Architecture diagram sample from the system-map cards
summary: A GitDiagram-style page of the five spines, hand-curated from the cards' reads/writes/invokes relations, Mermaid with GitHub click links plus a linked index; published as a private artifact for the maintainer to judge. The maintainer preferred it over graphify's graph. It is the target for PR-15.

title: Open proposals triaged; three-session track to 0.3.0-beta.1
summary: PR-15 (architecture diagram + graphctl) and PR-16 (CREDITS.md) filed; PR-6 (marketplace plugin) rejected on the maintainer's recorded direction. Next build session: six small fixes (PR-14, 16, 9, 10, 8, 5) then PR-15 by a builder in a worktree; then a review round (checklist 4, 10, 7, /adhd); then the beta. PR-11 and PR-4 after the beta holds; PR-1, PR-7, PR-12 stay condition-gated.

title: First PR-15 design followed the named tool, not the goal
summary: The research took graphify (the URL the maintainer sent) as the target and designed a function-level graph tab; when the maintainer saw graphify's output they named GitDiagram, a curated architecture diagram, as what they wanted. One design rewrite. A sample output shown before filing the proposal would have caught it in minutes (L-13).

title: uvx from an agent session is blocked; graphify extraction is a human-terminal step
summary: The auto-mode classifier denied the agent running uvx for an external package; the maintainer ran the extraction in their own terminal. Design choice: graphctl build prints the exact command and the ritual only normalises what exists; installing graphifyy once with uv tool makes a pinned binary that a narrow permission rule can name if the maintainer wants the ritual to run it.

title: L-12 recurred: the trimmed guide backticked the state folder
summary: The CLAUDE.md trim (PR-14) backticked .claude/state/ in the worker sentence; the home suite passed (the folder exists here) and the kit self-test failed on dev once the wave-1 merges landed, then stalled three wave-3 builders with the same failure. L-12's rule was a manual 'run context ritual dist before committing' and was not followed in full. Now mechanical: a fast test lints the shipped guide against the kit manifest.

title: Wave 3 shipped two defects the suite could not see
summary: The verifier found (1) POLISH would crash on the new graphctl generator because the verdict-tag map had no row for it, and (2) the graphify normaliser typed every class as a function on the real output while its fixture-based tests were green. Both fixed with tests the same session (L-14, L-15). The independent verifier pass after a wave is what caught them; it stays in the loop.

title: Build round wave 1: four fixes landed through builders in worktrees
summary: T14 accept removes the dispatch stub; T15 generator freshness compares output hashes and exit_build runs full-suite commands first; T16 obsctl analyze needs analyze.remote_consent for non-local endpoints and redacts key-shaped strings for every endpoint; T17 CREDITS.md ships in both kits. Each merged with statectl accept after the lead's diff review.

title: PR-5: settings.json deny rules cover only the universal denies
summary: Claude Code permissions.deny binds the main session and sub-agents alike, so the deny layer names only what every identity must never touch (the ritual ticket, the ritual hook, checkctl ticket, .claude-iff/); the protected tree stays gate-enforced. A parity test keeps the deny list in step with policy_gate.py's constants.

title: PR-14: CLAUDE.md trimmed to a map; template regenerated
summary: The root guide lost its duplicated protocol text; role sections and the Communication block stay because tests pin them. The 80-line target was unreachable without loosening those tests, recorded in the proposal resolution.

title: PR-15: code graph and architecture diagram (graphctl, mapctl architecture, console scope switcher)
summary: graphctl build|update|status normalises graphify output from the record root (or walks the repo with ast) into the gitignored code-graph store; mapctl architecture writes architecture.json (claude scope from the cards, tools scope from the graph) and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md as Mermaid with GitHub click links; the console MAP tab gained a scope switcher. Both are registered generators that run only in POLISH.

title: M-0.3.0-beta.1 build round complete; proposals PR-5/8/9/10/11/14/15/16 resolved
summary: Three waves merged into dev, an independent verifier pass on wave 3 found two defects that were fixed before closing, the suite is green and every task card has its envelope. Next: the human review round, then the beta cut from dev.

title: code-graph.json joined the gitignore-shadowing check's deliberate ignores
summary: The ritual's CHECK flagged the new lazy store as a shadowed shippable path: a gitignored file under .claude/ needs the managed block, the kit exclude list and checkctl's deliberate-ignore list, and only two of the three were done. Added with a test.

title: Human review round for 0.3.0-beta.1: items 4, 7, 10 run live; seven findings
summary: Console (item 4) clean. Worktree session (item 10): orientation, both refusals, the commit, the gate denial and the DONE.md advisory all held; the Cview paste gave 5 of 8 PASS, not 8. Fresh adoption (item 7) green on doctor and its first ritual; the extrct_private upgrade ended green only by a 3-way merge the skill does not describe. Findings PR-17 (session-start liveness probe), PR-18 (no .gitattributes in the kits), PR-19 (.cview/ and the worker sentence), PR-20 (dispatch/accept under Cview), PR-21 (upgrade path), PR-22 (lazy fold), PR-23 (fresh-kit test assumptions).

title: Beta.1 rulings: Cview refusal, relaxed Cview bar, history as evidence, one fix card, upgrade may fail
summary: Maintainer ruled: dispatch/accept refuse when .cview/ exists; the Cview box reads eight PASS after the kit's fixes and is not a release gate; items 1, 5, 6 count as evidenced by this repo's history with three boxes still to run live; one fix card done by the lead; the extrct_private upgrade runs once and a fail moves the criterion to the stable tag. Priority named: a workable system for dot-claude-iff users without breaking Cview.

title: extrct_private upgraded to alpha.2 by a 3-way merge, committed there
summary: 71 system files had diverged; the agent classified each against the source's git history and merged against the alpha.1 tag, replacing 70 old-upstream files, keeping 30 local ones, resolving 27 conflicts by rule. Its doctor and suite are green. The copy-only upgrade procedure could not have done this: PR-21 for the stable tag.

title: T21 beta.1 fix round: PR-12, 17, 18, 19, 20, 22 implemented, suite green
summary: _lib.pid_alive replaces os.kill(pid, 0) as the session-start liveness probe (Windows asks the kernel); both kits ship .gitattributes and doctor gained a gitattributes row; .cview/ in the managed gitignore block and the home .gitignore; the worker section tells a worker never to open the ritual or commit state from a worktree; statectl dispatch/accept refuse when .cview/ exists; cap_boxes keeps a fold of planned cards planned; the adhd upstream note owns the sonnet choice; the alpha checklist reworded in six places. Full suite green after one rework (see the mistake entry).

title: Two CHECK-time catches in the fix round: a backticked path the fresh kit lacks, and home paths in a task card
summary: The new worker sentence named .claude/state/ in backticks; the fresh kit ships no state folder, so the L-12 guide lint failed inside the kit self-test (two red tests, one rework to prose). The task card quoted two absolute sibling paths and no_machine_paths failed the first CHECK; made relative. Both mechanical checks did their job.

title: Suite step timeout raised to 1200 s for this repo
summary: CHECK's test_suite step timed out at 600 s: the full suite now runs about eleven minutes on the maintainer's machine, the kit self-test alone over five. The project step (memory.json, this repo only; the kits ship no project steps) now allows twenty minutes. Suite duration is a candidate for the PR-4 maturation pass.

title: CI on windows-latest red since 2026-11-05, fixed: graphctl resolves both sides of a repo-relative path
summary: Four pushes had a red Windows run nobody looked at. GitHub's runner names its temp folder by an 8.3 short name (RUNNER~1), so graphctl._repo_rel compared a resolved root against an unresolved absolute source_file and dropped every node; two test_graph tests and the kit self-test failed there only. Both sides are resolved now and a test spells the root through an alias (the short name on Windows, a symlink elsewhere). First green run since 2026-11-05 at 5cfdf92.

title: T21 verified live by the maintainer: Cview paste eight PASS, console URL at session start, items 1, 5, 6 boxes
summary: Fresh adoption from the rebuilt zip: no CRLF warnings on git add, doctor green with the new gitattributes row, Cview's eight requirements PASS with zero edits (E3 conditional on the .cview/ refusal, E4 on behaviour, both as ruled). A new session here printed the console URL while the console belonged to an earlier session. The three live boxes left from items 1, 5 and 6 passed in the fresh install: plain-words ritual refusal, deploy-phase proposal reflex, three sub-agent denials (PowerShell through Bash; no native PowerShell tool to test). Build signed off into review.

title: Two slips in the sign-off: a card status line the parser rejects, and a CI run nobody watched
summary: Closing T21 the agent wrote 'Status: done (2026-11-09)'; TASK_STATUS_LINE_RE wants the bare word, so the build exit check reported no card for T21 after a green ten-minute suite and the maintainer ran it twice. Separately, the Windows CI run had been red for four days across four pushes before the maintainer noticed; nothing in the ritual looks at CI (PR-24). Lessons L-17 and L-18.

title: Findings from the verification pass: PR-24 to PR-27
summary: PR-24 a ci_status row in CHECK; PR-25 the human cannot see the session-start block in the chat (ask the session to quote it; the checklist now says so); PR-26 the build exit check ran the full suite twice because one card's Test lacked -q and coverage compares commands literally; PR-27 a test leaks 'statectl need open' errors to stdout, shown under every exit-check row. Also raised, not filed: the release steps in the ritual are home-only (version stamp, parity, zips, workflow); an adopter's 'release vX' gets the procedure but no stamp of its own.

title: v0.3.0-beta.1 cut from dev: alpha checklist run end to end, fix round verified
summary: The maintainer named the version after the review sign-off. Stamp, citation and changelog section pinned; zips rebuilt on the release commit; tag pushed from dev so release.yml publishes the pre-release. Next: let it hold, then PR-21 (upgrade path), PR-23, the PR-4 maturation pass, merge to main, stable tag, PR-13 Zenodo.

title: consolectl.py stop: end the console a session start launched, so a folder can be deleted
summary: Retro P1 of the release ritual, approved by the maintainer as implement-now: Remove-Item on the throwaway repo failed because the kit's console held the folder, and eight console servers from various repos were running on the machine. The command reads the pidfile in the record root, ends the process, removes the file; it refuses a live pid whose console port is silent (a reused pid is not this console). Half the analyst's evidence was wrong (session-start already reuses a live console since PR-17) and was dropped.

title: doctor smart_app_control row: Windows 11 Smart App Control versus uv's unsigned Python
summary: The maintainer reported from a sibling project that Smart App Control moved to enforcing on this machine and blocked uv-managed Python builds and the venv launchers copied from them (astral-sh/uv#22869, open; the maintainers intend to sign, no date). Under that policy every hook, tool and the console die before printing a line. The row reads the policy state from the registry and, when enforcing, tells a uv-managed interpreter behind python3 from a python.org one by path and pyvenv.cfg, naming the remedy. Session start now prints one line when the console launch raised. This repo's python3 is the python.org build, so the row is OK here.
